sceneChange.fade: Crossfade — the previous one fades, this one appears
sceneChange.build: Build — the scene is there at once, its modules enter each in its own way
sceneChange.fly: Fly-through — the camera flies through the previous scene (its depth and word cloud)
sceneChange.rise: Rise — this one rises slightly from below
sceneChange.zoom: Zoom — the previous one grows and disappears, this one emerges from the depth
sceneChange.cover: Cover — this one slides up over the previous one
sceneChange.reveal: Reveal — the previous one slides up and reveals this one
sceneChange.side: From the side — this one slides in from the right, the previous one moves left
sceneChange.dissolve: Dissolve — the previous one fades, blurs and sinks, this one sharpens while rising (like the Cogita show)

arrival.fromLeft: Comes in past the left edge
arrival.fromRight: Comes in past the right edge

skin.plain: No background — just text, a logo, a picture
skin.panel: Panel — fills its rectangle with colour (and a picture)

textType.title: Title — capitals
textType.heading: Heading with text
textType.close: Punchline — accent-coloured italics, an empty line separates groups

format.screen: Full screen — like a start page (phone upright, with its own places)

font.spectral: Spectral + IBM Plex Sans (REcreatio start page)

progress.scene: Inside the scene — from the first to the last step
progress.enter: Scene entrance — the transition from the previous one
progress.leave: Scene exit — the transition to the next one

between.glide: Glides through the scenes in between
between.leave: Leaves with its scene and returns with the next

storyPage.needsAccess: [reference unavailable] This presentation is only for people with access.
storyPage.locked: [reference unavailable] This presentation is encrypted and this browser has no key for it.

unknownModule: The module “{kind}” is not known to this version of the page.

view.empty: This presentation has no scene yet.

map.title: Transitions between scenes
map.noWayIn: No button and no “next” leads to this scene — nobody will see it.
map.nextInList: the next one in the list ({target})
map.noModules: There are no modules on this scene.
map.linkLabel: Label (on the “next” button at the end)
map.addressHint: https://…, www.…, #/a page here, mailto:…, tel:…
map.help: Each scene has one entrance (on the left) and exits (on the right): “next” — arrows and scrolling — and one for each button. Drag from an exit to a scene, the end or a link. A dashed line — “next” leads to the next one in the list; delete it (Delete) to make this the end. Click a scene to choose targets from the list and make buttons; double-click opens the scene.
map.notLink: This is not an address that can be a link.

route.one: Without connections the presentation goes in order. The way without pressing buttons: {n} of {count} scene.
route.other: Without connections the presentation goes in order. The way without pressing buttons: {n} of {count} scenes.

editor.dropScene: Delete the scene “{name}”? The modules stay on the page; only their places on this scene disappear.
editor.empty: The presentation has no scene yet. A scene is one screen — modules stand on it where you put them.
editor.eachModule: Each module as its own scene
editor.arrange: Arrange all modules of this scene:
editor.arrangeBoth: Arrange all modules of this scene (at once on the narrow screen too):
editor.elsewhere: Modules of this page that are not here ({n})
editor.dropModule: Delete the module “{name}” from the page?
editor.presentHint: Full screen: arrows, space or a click — next; Esc — end
editor.previewHint: Preview — scroll in the frame (wheel, finger, arrows after clicking the frame). This is how a visitor will see it, without saving.
editor.arrangeHint: Click a module to choose it; drag the frame to move it; the handles change width and height. Arrows move it (with Shift — further), Alt turns off snapping.

story.naukaHint: The same course in Learning — in the knowledge base, next to its other courses (it points to this page, copies nothing)
story.title: Course — answers, conditions, values
story.answersWhere: Answers and the place where someone stopped
story.browserOnly: Only in the browser — an example; nothing leaves the device
story.inCogita: In Cogita — signed-in people (and people from a form) learn on their own account
story.base: Knowledge base in which the answers count
story.pickBase: Choose a knowledge base — until then the answers stay in the browser.
story.storage: Where the answers of signed-in people go
story.noAccount: Without an account the answers stay in the browser, as in the example. A person from a form counts only when an area is chosen (with intake).
story.off: Turn off the course (questions still check, but nothing is remembered)

progress.scene: Inside the scene (from the first to the last step)
progress.enter: Scene entrance (the transition from the previous one)
progress.leave: Scene exit (the transition to the next one)

settings.widthHint: The places of modules count within this width — on a wide screen the picture stays together (80 rem — like the Cogita show). The background stays on the whole screen.
settings.backdropHint: It stands behind all scenes. When there is one, the scenes are transparent and their own backgrounds (scene colour, its layers) lie in it and pass smoothly into each other — threads, waves and mist stay.
settings.soundHint: Plays only when the visitor clicks this button in the bar at the bottom — on a loop, quiet when the tab is hidden.
settings.volumeHint: Each scene can be quieter (scene settings).
settings.night: Other colours when the visitor’s device is in dark mode
settings.colorHint: A module’s colour can also be a pair “light|dark” (e.g. #ece0c9|#2a2113) or a name: accent, ink, ground, muted — then it follows the scene’s colours.
settings.sceneName: Name (in the scene bar; a link “#name” in a text leads here)
settings.change: How this scene replaces the previous one
settings.firstScene: This is the first scene — its transition is not visible.
settings.keep: The previous scene stays underneath until the transition ends
settings.jumpHint: How long the transition takes when an arrow or one turn of the wheel starts it.
settings.stepsHint: How many stops the scene has. A module with a step is then highlighted.
settings.branches: Branches, buttons and links outside — in the “Transitions” view.
settings.emphasis: Steps highlight their modules (the others fade and move back)
settings.grow: The scene grows as you go through it
settings.sceneVolumeHint: 1 — as in the whole presentation, 0 — silence on this scene; it changes smoothly between scenes.
settings.colorsEmpty: Empty — like the whole presentation. Also “light|dark”.
settings.depthHint: Modules with depth (z below zero) stand in the space of the scene. When the NEXT scene has the “Fly-through” transition, the camera flies through this scene — the nearer ones pass first, the deepest stays alone for a moment.
settings.flown: The next scene flies through this one.
settings.linger: Slow down at the deepest (the sentence stays alone for a moment)
settings.words: Word cloud — words (one per line; empty — no cloud)
settings.isButton: On this scene it is a button — a click leads on
settings.linksOutside: You add links outside in the “Transitions” view.
settings.everyHint: E.g. a fixed “Contact” button that stands on all scenes (with “Also stands before its first and after its last”). A target set separately for a scene takes precedence.
settings.sameTarget: The same target on every scene it stands on
settings.tallSame: On the narrow screen: as on the wide one — a change here makes a separate place.
settings.tallOwn: On the narrow screen: a separate place.
settings.maxWidth: At most this width (rem) — on a large screen it does not grow further
settings.zHint: 0 — flat. Below zero — into the depth of the scene (visible in a camera fly-through).
settings.motionHint: When the scene is reached (once) or over and over while visible — moves, grows, turns, fades in, draws; or a ready-made motion from the Cogita show.
settings.delayHint: The part of the transition after which it starts (0 — at once, 0.5 — halfway).
settings.spanHint: What part of the transition its appearance takes.
settings.travelHint: Tick the scenes on which the module has its place — when the scene changes it passes smoothly from one to the other (also through scenes without a place).
settings.hold: Also stands before its first and after its last place
settings.betweenHint: “Leaves and returns” — the same picture at the start and at the end of the story, and none in the middle; it then stands in the scene it is on, like its own module.
settings.leave: leaves with its scene and returns with the next
settings.layerHint: Higher — in front. A travelling one with a negative value (−1…−5) stands in front of the scene background but behind its texts; from 10 up — above all scenes.
settings.removeModule: Delete the module from the page
settings.cropHint: This point of the picture stays in view when the panel changes size (e.g. “50% 58%” — the focus). Empty — the point set in the picture module.
settings.radiusHint: 71 — reaches the corners when the centre is in the middle.
settings.frames: Frames — change with the scene’s progress
settings.progressHint: Scrolling (also backwards), the keyboard and the show move the same progress — stopped progress is a stopped picture.
settings.oneStep: The scene has one step — progress stays at 0. Add a step in the scene settings.
settings.framesHint: [{ "at": 0.4, "x": 30, "w": 40, "h": 55, "crop": "50% 60%" }, { "step": 2, "opacity": 0, "tall": { "y": 20 } }] — "at" 0–1 or "step" (from 0); a frame changes only what it gives; "tall" — its values on a phone.
settings.notFrames: — this is not a list of frames
settings.frameHere: + Frame at the end: the place as it is now
settings.stillHint: With the setting “reduce motion” the frames stand at one point (0–1) — a still composition with the same content. Empty: at the end (on exit — at the start); frames with steps jump from step to step.
